structured.approach: I read both inputs (task.code and feat.stories) and the backend-steps skill for BE-06. I used CodeGraph to see the exact source of the new functions and their callers; it reported that neither new function had any covering tests. I ran CI first to get a baseline: 3 tests, 71.4% coverage. I then added tests only in tests/test_aging.py, which is where TK-05.2 and SA-6 say they go. They cover every AC in AC-05.1–AC-05.10 and AC-06.1–AC-06.4, plus three more checks: the function doesn't change its inputs, the package exports, and empty input. All data is synthetic and uses the existing AS_OF date. I chose not to write tests for behaviour that still depends on open questions: bucket_for(30) (TQ-1), the rounding mode (DQ-2), the version (Q-2), and a missing vendor on a paid or not-yet-overdue invoice. I then re-ran CI until it passed, ran codegraph sync and codegraph affected, and wrote task.unit_tests.md.

claims.text: Before BE-06, CI ran 3 tests with 0 failures and total coverage of 71.4. Lines 22, 47-63 and 71 of src/ap_aging/aging.py were not covered, so CI failed.
After BE-06, CI compiles, runs 16 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors, and reports 100.0 coverage with no static issues. CI passes against the COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0 gate.
The only file this step changed is tests/test_aging.py. The existing AgingTest class and its tests are unchanged.
The boundary test checks that an unpaid invoice 31 days past due is listed and one exactly 30 days past due is not, as AC-05.1, AC-05.2 and lesson L-007 require.

The tests check that each row has exactly the keys id, vendor, days, amount and risk. They also check the sort order: days descending, then id ascending, so SYN-INV-002 comes before SYN-INV-003 on the 42-day tie (AC-05.5, AC-05.6).
Decimal("980.5") is checked to become Decimal("980.50"), and the CT-1 JSON amount is checked to be "1250.00", with no float conversion (AC-05.8, AC-06.2, D-2026-044, L-011).
AC-05.9 is checked by patching bucket_for so it raises if called, and confirming overdue_with_risk still returns its row.
overdue_with_risk reads inv["vendor"] only after the paid and threshold checks. So only an overdue unpaid invoice without vendor raises KeyError.
Every test name that task.code section 3 lists for BE-06 is now in tests/test_aging.py.

open_questions: UT-1 (non-blocking): AC-05.10 [Pending TQ-9] says any invoice with no vendor key raises KeyError. The code raises only for an overdue unpaid invoice. Which behaviour is intended? Architect (TQ-9) / PM.

UT-2 (non-blocking): codegraph affected reported 'No test files affected' for tests/test_aging.py and src/ap_aging/aging.py, even though the test file imports aging. I ran the full CI instead. Platform team (CodeGraph).
Carried unchanged: task.code Q-2 (confirm version 1.5.0), PQ-2, TQ-1 (bucket_for(30) left untested on purpose), TQ-3, TQ-9, DQ-2 (rounding mode not tested), CQ-6.
structured.summary: I added 13 unit tests to ap_aging tests/test_aging.py, covering overdue_with_risk (AC-05.1–AC-05.10) and overdue_rows_to_json (AC-06.1–AC-06.4). CI now passes: 16 tests, 0 failures, 100.0% coverage (it was 71.4%), and no static issues. This clears task.code Q-1. The tests don't cover behaviour that still waits on open questions (TQ-1, DQ-2, Q-2), and UT-1 asks whether the KeyError in AC-05.10 should apply to every invoice without a vendor. The output is written to task.unit_tests.md. Nothing has been committed.
